card.title: RAAF HURRICANE TROP
card.text: Deployment: Gets +1+1 and Blitz if deployed from right-most in hand.
card.flavorText: The Hawker Hurricane served with the RAAF mostly overseas, rather than for home defence in Australia. In 1941 and 1942, No. 3 Squadron RAAF, No. 450 Squadron RAAF, and No. 451 Squadron RAAF all used RAF numbered Hurricanes in the Middle East. These aircraft were not Australian-built or uniquely marked RAAF machines, but they were flown and maintained by Australian units in active service. No. 3 Squadron RAAF converted to Hurricanes in North Africa in early 1941. The squadron used them as fighters and for ground attack during the desert campaign, before changing to P-40 Tomahawks later. No. 450 Squadron RAAF also used Hurricanes while forming an operational squadron in the Middle East. No. 451 Squadron RAAF had a detachment that operated Hurricanes during the Siege of Tobruk, including reconnaissance work. Only one Hurricane served on Australian soil. It was a tropicalised Hurricane Mk I given to Australia by Britain in 1941, numbered V7476. It received the RAAF serial A60-1 and was used for familiarization, communications, public demonstrations, and testing Professor Frank Cotton’s anti-G suit at Laverton base in 1942.
